- Snake moves continuously in one of 4 directions (up/down/left/right), grows when eating food
- Game ends on wall collision or self-collision
- Keyboard controls for player movement
- CPU-controlled snake mode that automatically searches for food (pathfinding - simple BFS toward food while avoiding walls and self; if no path, follow a safe direction)
- Three game modes selectable from a start menu:
  1. Human vs Human (P1: WASD or Arrow keys, P2: IJKL keys)
  2. CPU vs Human (P1: CPU, P2: WASD/Arrows)
  3. CPU vs CPU (both CPU)
- Display score during gameplay (each snake's score and length)
- Start menu screen with title, instructions, and mode selection (use number keys 1/2/3 or click buttons)
- Game over screen showing winner, scores, and restart prompt
- Restart with keypress (Space or R) - restart returns to start menu OR restarts same mode
- Visually appealing: dark background, neon-style snakes (P1 green, P2 magenta/purple), red food, grid lines subtle
- Smooth animation using requestAnimationFrame with a fixed tick rate (e.g., 8-10 moves per second)
- Food should never spawn on a snake body
- CPU snakes must not collide with walls, themselves, OR the other snake
- When a snake dies (collides), it's removed and the other snake wins (or it's a draw if both die same tick)
- Show "PAUSED" overlay if needed (optional)

CODE STRUCTURE:
- Wrap everything in a single <script> at end of body
- Use a Game class or module pattern with:
  - Constants: GRID_SIZE=30, CELL_SIZE (e.g., 20px so canvas is 600x600)
  - Snake objects: { body: [{x,y},...], dir: {x,y}, nextDir, alive, score, isCpu, color, controls }
  - Food: {x, y}
  - State: 'menu' | 'playing' | 'gameover'
  - Mode: 'hvh' | 'cvh' | 'cvc'
- Input handler maps keys to snake direction changes (prevent 180-degree reversal)
- CPU AI: BFS shortest path to food on the grid, considering the snake's own body and the other snake's body as obstacles. If path is found, set next direction toward first step. If no path, pick the direction that maximizes survival (e.g., follow tail or any non-lethal direction).
- Game loop: tick at fixed interval, update positions, check collisions, spawn food, render to canvas
- Render: clear canvas, draw grid (faint), draw food (red circle/square), draw both snakes (rounded segments with head distinct), draw HUD with scores

STYLING:
- Center the canvas on page
- Use a Google Font (e.g., 'Press Start 2P' or 'Orbitron') for retro game feel
- Title screen with large title, mode buttons styled as cards
- Game over screen as overlay on canvas
- Use CSS variables for colors
- Responsive: canvas stays 600x600, page has padding

Make sure the game is fully playable, all three modes work, CPU snakes are reasonably smart (BFS pathfinding), and the UI is polished. Include clear on-screen instructions for controls.

Output the complete HTML file content."}
